record.paper_title: Opportunities and open questions in modern β decay
record.original_question: How can lattice-QCD calculations of the nucleon axial charge gA control excited-state contamination, pion-mass extrapolation, finite-volume effects, and continuum extrapolation well enough to reach roughly 0.5% precision with current computer architecture and about 0.2% precision in the exascale-computing era?

evidence.quote: While extrapolations to the physical pion mass can be made using chiral perturbation theory, their convergence properties are unclear and modern FLAG summaries consider only calculations with at least one point at the physical pion mass for their global averages (91).
Excited state contaminations (ESC) were found to be a major culprit and remain the predominant concern to this day (91, 93, 94, 95, 96).
Efforts have been proposed to reach an 0.5% precision with current computer architecture and down to 0.2% in the exascale computing era.

artifact.status_search_result: Current state-of-the-art lattice-QCD determinations of $g_A$ reach roughly 1% total uncertainty (e.g., CalLat's Nature 2018 result $g_A = 1.271(13)$, and recent percent-level calculations). FLAG-style averages still rely on a handful of physical-pion-mass ensembles, and excited-state ($\pi N$) contamination remains the dominant systematic; recent (2025) methodological work explicitly targets removing $\pi N$-state contamination. No published calculation has yet demonstrated 0.5% (let alone 0.2%) total precision, so the goal remains an open programmatic target for current and exascale computing.

status_evidence.title: A per-cent-level determination of the nucleon axial coupling from QCD (Nature 2018)
status_evidence.snippet: Theoretical determination of the nucleon axial coupling with a precision of one per cent, giving 1.271 ± 0.013.
status_evidence.claim: Best published precision is at the ~1% level, not yet 0.5%.

status_evidence.title: Method for high-precision determination of the nucleon axial structure using lattice QCD: Removing πN-state contamination (2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Method proposed for removing πN-state contamination in nucleon axial structure lattice calculations.
status_evidence.claim: Excited-state (πN) contamination is still the dominant systematic being actively addressed in 2025.

status_evidence.title: Precision Nucleon Charges and Form Factors Using 2+1-flavor Lattice QCD
status_evidence.snippet: Recent precision lattice determinations of nucleon charges still report few-percent uncertainties.
status_evidence.claim: Sub-0.5% precision target has not yet been achieved.
